months.headline: Plan & rest
months.bottomLine: Rest the lawn, order seed, and get a soil test in before the spring rush.
months.summary: Stay off frozen grass, use lawn-safe ice melt near turf, prune oaks while it's safe, and plan the year: seed order, soil test and mower tune-up.

months.headline: Prep
months.bottomLine: Tune up the mower, start broccoli and cabbage indoors, and cut back ornamental grasses late in the month.
months.summary: Prune summer-flowering shrubs and dormant trees, set up grow lights, and clean the rain barrel. The lawn needs nothing yet; skip the early-spring fertilizer.

months.headline: Wake up
months.bottomLine: Clean up gently, plant peas, potatoes and onions, and have crabgrass preventer ready for redbud bloom.
months.summary: Rake out winter debris, start tomatoes and peppers indoors, and sow cool-season crops as soon as the soil crumbles. Wait for highs in the 50s before a big bed cleanup. Stop pruning oaks by mid-March.

months.headline: Pre-emergent month
months.bottomLine: Crabgrass preventer by redbud bloom (by April 15), start mowing at 3–3.5 in, and keep planting cool crops.
months.summary: One application of prodiamine or dithiopyr stops crabgrass all season. Skip it where you seeded. Divide summer perennials, harden off transplants, and put up the rabbit fence.

months.headline: Big planting month
months.bottomLine: Plant tomatoes, peppers and melons after about May 10. No lawn fertilizer from here until September.
months.summary: Warm crops go in as soil hits 60–65°F. Mulch the garden, lay soaker hose, and prune spring-flowering shrubs after bloom. Apply grub preventer only if you had grubs last year.

months.headline: Mow high
months.bottomLine: Raise the mower to 4 in, protect squash from vine borers, and harvest garlic and peas.
months.summary: Watch for brown patch as nights warm, hand-pick Japanese beetles (no traps), scout tomatoes for early blight, and start fall broccoli mid-month.

months.headline: Survival mode
months.bottomLine: Let the lawn rest: mow high, stay off it, water only by the 3-week rule, and sow the fall garden late in the month.
months.summary: Tall fescue browns in heat and drought, and that's normal. Soak ½–1 in only after about 3 weeks without ½ in of rain in the heat. Check for grubs if patches peel back like carpet. Pick vegetables often.

months.headline: Get ready
months.bottomLine: Buy fall grass seed, kill bermuda patches, plant fall greens, and wake a dormant lawn late in the month.
months.summary: Read seed tags and buy a 90/10 tall fescue–bluegrass blend, spot-spray bermudagrass so it's dead by seeding time, sow lettuce and spinach, and order spring bulbs.

months.headline: The most important lawn month
months.bottomLine: Aerate, overseed, feed. The most important lawn month.
months.summary: Core aerate and overseed around Labor Day, feed 1–1.5 lb N, and start fall broadleaf weed control once new grass has been mowed 3 times. Divide perennials, plant trees and shrubs, and dig sweet potatoes.

months.headline: Second feeding & garlic
months.bottomLine: Feed the lawn again (1 lb N) in mid-October, mulch-mow the leaves, and plant garlic and spring bulbs.
months.summary: October 10–15 is the practical cutoff for seeding. First mow new grass at 3 in. Sow a cover crop on empty beds, pull frosted vines, and drain the hoses before the first hard freeze.

months.headline: Winterize
months.bottomLine: Final lawn feeding (quick-release N) and a broadleaf spray, then winterize the mower, hoses and young tree trunks.
months.summary: Winterizer nitrogen feeds roots for an early spring green-up. Spray dandelions and clover on a 50°F day, put hardware-cloth guards on young trees, and cut invasive bush honeysuckle while it's still green.

months.headline: Rest & review
months.bottomLine: Stay off frozen grass, review your journal, and plan next year's garden rotation.
months.summary: Mound mulch over rose crowns, check the garlic mulch, service tools, and put a soil probe, rain gauge or hose timer on your wish list.

seasons.name: Winter
seasons.lawn: Stay off frozen turf, get a soil test, sharpen the mower blade, plan the nitrogen budget.
seasons.beds: Leave stems and seed heads for birds and bees. Prune dormant trees and summer-flowering shrubs.
seasons.veg: Order seed, plan rotation, start onions (January) and broccoli/cabbage (February) under lights.
seasons.yard: Prune oaks (safe window), check trunk guards, clean tools and the rain barrel.

seasons.name: Spring
seasons.lawn: Crabgrass preventer at redbud bloom; little or no nitrogen; mow at 3–3.5 in.
seasons.beds: Cut back grasses, clean up once highs hold in the 50s, mulch 2–3 in, divide summer and fall bloomers.
seasons.veg: Cool crops from mid-March; warm crops from about May 10; mulch and drip lines in late May.
seasons.yard: Ticks and chiggers arrive; mosquito control starts; treat ash for EAB if you're protecting one.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.lawn: Mow at 4 in; survival watering only (3-week rule); watch for grubs and brown patch.
seasons.beds: Water new plantings weekly, deadhead, hand-pick Japanese beetles, pinch mums until July 4.
seasons.veg: Harvest often; fight squash vine borers; sow the fall garden late July–August.
seasons.yard: Water young trees in dry spells; dump standing water weekly.

seasons.name: Fall
seasons.lawn: Aerate and overseed around Labor Day; feed in Sep, Oct and Nov; broadleaf weed control.
seasons.beds: Plant perennials, shrubs, trees and bulbs; divide perennials; leave the leaves in beds.
seasons.veg: Plant garlic in October, sow cover crops, clean up diseased vines, harvest cold-hardy greens.
seasons.yard: Mulch-mow leaves, drain hoses, winterize the mower, guard young trunks.
